newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Ugandan troops patrol Zairean border town.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan troops patrol Zairean border town.

text.p: Ugandan troops patrolled a town 10 km (six miles) inside Zaire on Thursday after driving out what Uganda says are mainly Moslem rebels backed by the Islamist government in Khartoum.
An army spokesman in the nearby Ugandan town of Kasese had said fighting continued in the area on Thursday after the Ugandan army killed 50 of the rebels on Wednesday.
But Kasindi and villages on the Ugandan side of the border were quiet on Thursday afternoon and there was no sign of the rebels of the Allied Democratic Force (ADF).
A local commander said his troops would leave Zaire in two days. His superiors in Kampala had said the troops came back last week after a brief incursion.
"UPDF (Ugandan government) troops will pull out of Zaire in two days' time. We have crushed the rebels and it is time to go home," said the commander, who declined to be named.
"But the Zairean government must give us assurances that rebels will not continue attacking us from Zaire," he added.

The government in Kampala, however, recognises that Kinshasa has lost control of much of eastern Zaire to Zairean rebels. Kampala has blamed Sudanese Islamist leader Hassan al-Turabi for the anti-Ugandan rebel activity.
The ADF rebels, an obscure group that first hit the headlines last month, appear to have taken advantage of the chaos in eastern Zaire to launch attacks into Uganda.

The Zairean rebel group, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), has swept north parallel to the Ugandan border but did not appear to have come into contact with the Ugandan rebels.
Uganda has repeatedly denied Zairean government accusations that, together with Rwanda and Burundi, it has sent troops to fight alongside the Zairean rebels.

Travellers reaching Kasindi on Thursday said the Zairean rebels had moved on from the town of Beni, 55 km (35 miles) north of Kasindi, and were advancing towards the much larger towns of Watsa, Isiro and Kisangani, the regional capital.
